title: Redwood Console: Tracing, Error Analysis & Request Logs - Walkthrough (Acme Payments)
summary: Sales demo focused on Redwood Console tracing and request logs for debugging production errors. Customer (Acme Payments) is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for latency-sensitive payment flows, had questions about PII in logs, retention, SSO, and canary rollouts. SE showed traces, error analysis, and how to pivot from an error in the trace to a request log and payload. Next steps: share security pack, pricing for a 3-month pilot (dedicated), and schedule benchmark run with sample traffic.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Acme), Maria Gomez (Platform Eng), Noah Patel (SRE), Sana Rahman (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Liam: Liam here, CTO at Acme Payments. We're evaluating inference infra for our fraud scoring model, mostly really interested in observability.
[00:15] Maria: Maria, platform, want to understand traces and request logs, retention, and PII handling.
[00:20] Noah: Noah, SRE, curious about debugging flow and how we triage latency spikes.
[00:24] Sana: Sana, security, SOC2 questions and KMS integration.
[00:29] Priya: Awesome, thanks. We'll do a live walkthrough of the Console \u2014 tracing, error analysis, request logs \u2014 and show a typical debugging flow from trace to payload. We'll keep it high level and then go deep where needed.
[00:45] Jordan: Also quick administrative note \u2014 we'll share the security pack and benchmark run plan after. If you want, Priya can start with the tracing view.

[01:02] Priya: Okay sharing screen \u2014 should be seeing the Redwood Console, Traces page. The UI groups traces by endpoint, model, and time bucket. Here's a sample trace for our chat inference route, you can see span breakdowns for scheduler, kv-cache lookup, tokenization, model execution.
[01:25] Maria: Sorry can you zoom into the kv-cache bit? We saw a lot of cache misses in our pilot and wondering how Redwood surfaces that.
[01:32] Priya: Yeah, good point. So each span has metadata tags \u2014 you can see "cache_hit: false" here, and we also show approximate latency contribution. If you click into the span we link to the related request log id.
[01:45] Noah: That link \u2014 is that the full request with input payload? How does that work for PII-sensitive tokens?
[01:52] Priya: By default the request log will contain metadata and a hashed/scrubbed payload preview. For customers that need full payloads for internal debugging we support role-based access and configurable PII redaction. You can also set retention policies per project.
[02:08] Sana: When you say hashed, is that reversible? We need to prove that sensitive fields aren't stored elsewhere.
[02:15] Priya: It's a one-way hash for default scrubbing. For enterprise Dedicated or Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS so you control keys and decryption \u2014 but Redwood's hosted offering never stores raw sensitive fields unencrypted. We'll include the SOC2 docs in the pack.

[02:34] Jordan: Quick interjection \u2014 Acme mentioned dedicated vs hosted earlier, are you leaning one way?
[02:39] Liam: We're leaning Dedicated for latency predictability and data residency, but wanted to see the debug experience first.
[02:45] Jordan: Makes sense. Priya, continue.

[02:52] Priya: Back to the trace \u2014 here's an error span at the model step showing a timeout error, code 504. You can click to see error details and the full stack. We also auto-correlate rate-limit and quota events so you can see root cause \u2014 e.g., scheduler backpressure leading to queue timeouts.
[03:12] Maria: Is there alerting tied to those errors? Can I create an alert if 504s exceed X%?
[03:17] Priya: Yes, Console integrates with alerts \u2014 you can set thresholds at service or route level and route alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. We also have anomaly detection suggestions via Redwood Optimize but that's an add-on.
[03:27] Noah: If I have a flame graph of span durations can I compare across deployments or model versions?
[03:33] Priya: Yep, per-route dashboards let you compare model versions and hardware. You can pin a baseline and see regression traces.

[03:45] [04:00] Priya: Now clicking the error span link to the request log. This opens the request detail page \u2014 it shows request id, timing breakdown, headers, model version, route config, and a scrubbed input preview. There's also a downloadable full log if you have access.
[04:22] Liam: How long are those logs retained? We need 90 days for audits.
[04:27] Priya: Retention is configurable. Hosted customers can pick tiers (30/90/365 days). For Dedicated, retention is configurable and can be backed by your storage. We'll put the exact SLAs in the security pack.
[04:39] Sana: Can we prove deletion? For GDPR/DSAR requests we need to know data is purged on request.
[04:45] Priya: Yes, we have a deletion workflow with audit logs. Deletions emit an event you can export to your SIEM. Again, we'll include the process doc.

[04:58] [05:15] Priya: Demoing the request timeline \u2014 you can jump from an error sample to all requests with similar signatures and replay them against a sandbox model for debugging. That replay is isolated and doesn't hit production keys.
[05:33] Maria: Replay sounds useful. Is the replay deterministic with the same model version and kernel selection?
[05:39] Priya: We try to ensure parity; we surface model version, quantization profile, and runtime config used at the time of the original request. For Dedicated, you control the pinned kernel selection. For hosted, Redwood picks kernel choices but we report them in the trace metadata.

[05:58] Noah: On sampling \u2014 do you sample every trace or only errors? We have high QPS so full tracing could be costly.
[06:06] Priya: Sampling is configurable \u2014 you can do 100% for errors, 10% for success, or use dynamic sampling where we increase sampling around anomalies. Sampling decisions are logged so you can correlate metrics later.

[06:22] [06:30] Jordan: Jumping to question from Maria in chat \u2014 will request logs include headers like Authorization?
[06:36] Priya: No, auth headers are redacted by default. You can configure the scrubber rules but Redwood's default blocks common sensitive headers.

[06:45] [07:00] Liam: What about integration with our existing tracing stack \u2014 we use Jaeger + DataDog. Can we export traces?
[07:08] Priya: We provide export hooks and can push spans to your tracing backend or export via OTLP. There's also an API to pull request logs and traces for your retention pipeline.

[07:20] Maria: Is there RBAC around who can see the full payloads?
[07:25] Priya: Yes, Console has RBAC. You can create roles like "can_view_payloads" and tie them to SSO groups via SAML. For critical data we recommend combining RBAC with KMS-controlled decryption.

[07:38] [08:00] Sana: On SOC2 \u2014 are you certified? We saw some of your security pages but need the report for procurement.
[08:06] Jordan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. We'll share the audit report and the security pack after the call.

[08:18] Priya: Moving to a debugging scenario \u2014 say you see an uptick in latency. We'd look at traces, identify the high-latency span (e.g., model execution), then pivot to request logs to inspect payload sizes and input distributions. Here I'm filtering by route and model version and we can see larger batch sizes correlating with higher queue times.
[08:44] Maria: Can we set automatic mitigation? Like auto-fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes?
[08:50] Priya: Yes, that's part of Smart Routing and automatic fallback policies \u2014 you can define a policy to route to a smaller model or Dedicated burst pool when latency exceeds thresholds.

[09:05] [09:30] Noah: For the benchmarking you mentioned, do you support synthetic workloads and can you replay production traffic?
[09:36] Priya: We support both. For production replay we scrub PII and run in a sandbox. For synthetic, we have a load harness and recommend a 24-72 hour run to capture tail latencies. We'll provide a plan template.

[09:50] Liam: Any known limitations for our use case \u2014 real-time fraud scoring with a 50ms p95 target?
[09:58] Priya: For 50ms p95 you typically need Dedicated capacity with optimized batching disabled for those routes. Our SDK allows per-route config to prioritize latency. We'll include recommended instance types and quantization profiles.

[10:10] [10:30] Jordan: Quick note on pricing for pilots \u2014 we can do a three-month Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity. I'll send a ballpark, then we can do a formal quote with engineering details once we run the benchmark.

[10:40] Priya: Wrapping up the live demo \u2014 I'm going to show one more thing: the Error Analysis view which aggregates error types, root causes, and suggested remediations (e.g., reduce batch size, increase timeout). It links directly to traces and request logs for triage.
[11:00] Maria: That's handy. Can error taxonomy be customized?
[11:03] Priya: Yes, you can add custom error classes and map certain exception messages to them. We also allow exporting the taxonomy for programmatic alerting.

[11:18] [11:30] Jordan: Let's go to Q&A and next steps.
[11:32] Liam: Two quick asks \u2014 1) share SOC2 + KMS integration docs, 2) sample retention config for 90 days and export options.
[11:40] Sana: Also need a description of the deletion/audit workflow for DSARs.
[11:45] Jordan: We'll send all of that. Also, can we schedule the benchmark run next week?
[11:50] Maria: Week of Jan 4 works for us, we need to align infra access.
[11:54] Noah: I'll be the technical lead on the benchmark.
[11:58] Jordan: Great \u2014 we'll draft a runbook and share.

[12:05] Priya: Last note \u2014 for debugging we recommend instrumenting the SDK to emit route-level metrics and sample traces. That gives the best correlation between metrics and traces.
[12:15] Jordan: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack, pilot pricing, and a benchmark runbook.
[12:24] Liam: Thanks all, this was helpful.

End of transcript
